strengths: Introduces a well-motivated and practically useful idea: restricting OSM watermarking to a specific sub-domain to simultaneously preserve generation quality/persistence (unlike full-coverage watermarks) while retaining the strong statistical guarantees of watermark-based detection for fingerprinting purposes.

Clearly articulates a set of practical desiderata for fingerprinting (reliability, persistence, stealthiness, harmlessness, robustness) grounded in prior work, and systematically evaluates the method against each.

Extensive empirical evaluation across two model families (Llama3.2-1B, Qwen2.5-3B/7B) and three domains (Math, Health, French), covering detection reliability with formal p-value guarantees, quality preservation (perplexity, GPT-4 judge, benchmark accuracy), persistence under multiple finetuning scenarios, and robustness to system prompts/sampling strategies.

Direct empirical comparison against two backdoor-based fingerprinting baselines (instructional fingerprinting, scalable fingerprinting), showing clear practical advantages in robustness to system prompts and persistence under finetuning — this strengthens the paper's claims of superiority over existing approaches.

Rich set of supplementary analyses in the appendix (watermark tokens as domain triggers, multiple simultaneous watermark keys, domain-leakage sensitivity study, watermarking a harmful-content domain) that explore the boundaries and practical considerations of the approach, going beyond a minimal viable evaluation.

Good use of the monotonicity property of watermark-based statistics to argue that detection power can be recovered via additional queries even when signal is weakened, which is empirically demonstrated.
weaknesses: The method's core threat model implicitly assumes the adversary will naturally be queried/triggered into generating target-domain content; if a deployer restricts or filters domain-specific queries (intentionally or not) or the domain never naturally arises in their use case, the fingerprint may never be triggered — this fundamental limitation is not deeply analyzed.

Persistence against in-domain (worst-case adversarial) finetuning degrades substantially, and for the Math domain on Qwen2.5-3B the paper explicitly states the signal cannot be recovered at all even with more queries — a nontrivial gap not fully resolved by the monotonicity argument.

Sensitivity to domain leakage between regularization and target datasets is a real limitation acknowledged by the authors; in practice, guaranteeing clean separation for arbitrary real-world domains may be difficult, and this could undermine the harmlessness/specificity guarantees.

Only one watermarking scheme (KGW logit-distillation) is evaluated; generalization to other OSM watermarking families (weight-perturbation, joint classifier-based) mentioned in related work is not empirically tested.

Model scale is modest (1B–7B parameters); it is unclear whether findings (e.g., ease of domain-specific behavior learning, quality preservation) transfer to larger, more capable open models that are more likely to be commercially valuable targets for fingerprinting.

Stealthiness claims rely on qualitative examples and comparison rather than a rigorous quantitative detectability/distinguishability metric against an adaptive adversary attempting to identify or filter domain-specific watermark queries.

No evaluation against more sophisticated/adaptive adversaries (e.g., model deployers aware of the domain-specific watermarking technique who might specifically try to suppress or filter suspected trigger domains), which is a realistic concern given the threat model of restrictive licensing disputes.

strengths: Novel and well-motivated paradigm shift from brittle query-key fingerprinting to semantic-domain-conditioned statistical watermarking, addressing genuine limitations of prior work (IF, SF) in a principled way.

Extensive empirical evaluation across 3 model families/sizes, 25+ deployment scenarios (sampling, quantization, pruning, finetuning) and 5 targeted adversarial scenarios, consistently showing 100% FSR for the proposed method versus frequent failures of baselines.

Rigorous theoretical grounding: Theorem D.1 proves the Z-test statistic for concatenated multi-query detection is asymptotically standard normal, giving proper FPR control even with an added correction term beyond prior work.

Thoughtful ablations covering number of queries, semantic domain choice/entropy, watermark strength δ (utility/detectability tradeoff), and the effect of the regularization loss, which strengthen the credibility of design choices.
Reasonable effort to establish stealthiness quantitatively via an LLM-judge classifier, showing the method is far less detectable than IF and comparable to SF for inputs while remaining more robust.

Additional exploratory contributions (watermark tokens, multi-key domains, harmful-content watermarking) that expand the applicability and show extensibility of the core idea beyond the main use case.
Good reproducibility effort: detailed hyperparameters, dataset/model licensing, resource usage, and algorithm pseudocode provided.
weaknesses: Main experiments rely heavily on a single semantic domain (French) as the primary showcase; while other domains are explored in appendices, the core narrative and most robustness claims are drawn from one setting, raising some concern about generality across languages/domains with different entropy characteristics.

Fingerprint detection cost scales with number of queries (up to 1000), and while cheap in dollar terms, this assumes the malicious deployer allows large-scale free querying without rate-limiting/cost countermeasures, which is not deeply discussed as a practical adversarial response.

Table 4 shows a non-trivial drop in LLM-as-judge quality scores within the semantic domain (e.g., LLAMA3.2-1B French score drops from 5.10 to 3.18), which, though framed as acceptable, could be a meaningful stealth/utility concern not fully reconciled with the stealth claims.

Stealth evaluation relies on a single GPT5-MINI judge with prompts chosen by the authors to minimize FPR; a more adversarial or diverse set of detectors (including ones aware of the semantic-domain concept) would strengthen the stealth claims, and the paper's own limitation section acknowledges detection is possible if the domain is known.

Model sizes tested are modest (1B–8B parameters); it is unclear how well the method scales to larger, more capable models or whether distillation-based watermark embedding remains as effective/harmless at scale.

The comparison baselines (IF, SF) were originally designed for the completion setting and adapted by the authors to the instruction-tuning setting, which could raise questions about whether the baselines were optimally tuned/implemented for a fair comparison.
